THE MATERIAL CLAIM IS NONETHELESS PROVEN by three sibling steps that DID go green in the same run: `mounted` ('the harness recorded a write call for the code path'), `codeNotWritten` ('the denied code path was never created'), and the falsifiable pair `controlNotDenied` + `controlWritten` ('with verify.mode=off the same write was not refused' / 'the code path really was written').
findings.expected: Reduce the conjunct to exactly `write.called && !write.succeeded` — that IS the right evidence for 'the block is real', because a PRE-DISPATCH guard refusal cannot produce a `tool/result` frame carrying the sentence (the writer's own finding), while the sentence is demonstrably visible in the model transcript (`run-a-guarded.log` quotes it verbatim: 'Error: verification law: `write` on the CODE path … is refused …'). Keep the sentence as a RECORDED secondary signal, never as a conjunct of `ok`; then re-run to 9/9 and take THAT run as the live evidence. Answering the two questions asked directly: (a) YES, `called && !succeeded` is the right evidence — it is the material fact and no prose can fake it; (b) YES, the `verify.mode=off` control genuinely falsifies — the SAME write against the SAME path lands when the guard is off and is absent when it is on, which is a two-way, self-contained falsification.
